question: Will Pete Hegseth still be serving as U.S. Secretary of Defense on November 12, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Status quo: Hegseth holds office as of Nov 2 and the window is only ~10.8 days. Removal can only come through resignation or firing; a Senate impeachment trial can't finish in time, and the Blackburn Senate-seat exit can't happen before January 2027. Trump defended him Oct 29 and his team says he will stay. Pressure spikes after the Nov 3 midterms and Massie's push when the House returns Nov 9. Polymarket 'out by Nov 30' trades ~21% ($52k volume) and 'out by Dec 31' ~30% ($966k). These near-miss contracts have later deadlines; scaling to Nov 12 with front-loading gives ~8-12% out.

- Resolves off defense.gov/About/Leadership (else credible sources); an announcement of a future departure does not count; temporary delegation to Feinberg does not count.
- Event window: now -> 2026-11-12 23:00 UTC; the question opened before the midterms, and ~10.8 days remain as of Nov 2.
- Searched but not found: a Kalshi market; midterm results (not yet held); any reported successor vetting.

calls.reconciliation: No factual disputes: all three runs agree he is in office, the impeachment and Blackburn paths cannot complete before Nov 12, Trump defended him Oct 29, and the Polymarket Nov 30 and Dec 31 prices match the harness data. The only dispute is judgment: how much of the ~20% Nov 30 Polymarket risk falls in the first ~11 of 28 days. An even spread gives ~8%; risk is front-loaded by the midterm and the Massie vote (Sessions precedent), offset by Trump's resistance to firing under pressure. I'd bet on ~11% out, i.e. 0.89. The Manifold Dec 31 market (0.70 to stay) agrees with Polymarket. No web retrieval this run.
